title: What is the longest film you have ever seen?

commenti.body: The Works and Days (of Tayoko Shiojiri in the Shiotani Basin) (2020) - a very serene 8-hour film, that I admittedly watched in segments over the course of about a week. The IMDb description has it as: "A geographic description of fourteen months of the work and non-work of Tayoko in the mountains of Kyoto Prefecture, Japan." Which is true, there are a lot of long lingering shots of just the scenery of the mountains, and it's stunning. Just don't be tired while watching because it will put you to sleep.

Satantango is certainly a staple of long cinema, and a favorite of mine. 

If you like documentary, check out Wang Bing’s Tie Xi Qu: West of the tracks. It’s 9 hours, and deeply moving. Also, Shoah. 

Lav Diaz is another great filmmaker known for long films. Most sit around the 5-8 hour mark, and all are wonderful. “From what is before” is my favorite I’ve seen of his. 

Edward Yang’s Brighter Summer Day is shorter, only around 4 hours, but very masterfully made as a coming of age. 

The late Hu Bo, a successor to Bela Tarr in many ways, only made one film before his passing — An Elephant Sitting Still — but it is remarkable. Around 4 hours as well if I remember.

Evolution of a Filipino Family by Lav Diaz at 10h at 25 mins is the longest I’ve seen. 
After that there are some Wang Bing like West of the Tracks at 9h, few other Lav films, The Works and Days, Satantango and more.

OJ: Made in America

At 467 minutes it is the longest film to ever win an Oscar. I saw it when it was edited into a miniseries format, but I'm still counting it. 

Frankly, I think any movie over 3 hours should be broken up into parts. Any longer and you are just watching a miniseries edited together. One of my favorite movies of all time is Kill Bill, which was intended to be a single long movie. The Whole Bloody Affair is 250min. 

You could also call Lord of the Rings one long film since it's all one long production.

I do not know long it is but Prince of the City by Sidney Lumet is longest film I have ever seen. Bloody brilliant police drama though. Just watching Treat Williams go through a rollercoster of events and constantly battling with himself if he is doing the right thing, I didnt want it to end.

I think it depends on the intended way to view it by the director. If the intention is to watch it in one session in the cinema (the behemoths often has one or more intermissions though) it’s not a miniseries. Of course it doesn’t stop you from treating it like a mini-series when watching it at home. :)
